Chapter 2: Acting Decisively—The Power of Doing Over Deliberating
Let’s take a moment to think about what separates truly outstanding companies from the rest. One thing you’ll notice right away is their relentless drive to get things done. In a world where uncertainty is more common than certainty, waiting around for perfect information—or for everyone to agree—can leave you stuck. That’s why these companies focus on action. They’d rather move forward and learn along the way, than get bogged down chasing perfection.
Picture a company as a living, breathing organism. Just like our bodies need to move and adapt, organizations thrive when people are encouraged to try things out, test new ideas, and respond quickly when things change. What does that look like day to day? Well, it means teams are trusted to make decisions right where the work happens. People closest to the action are empowered to take initiative—without waiting for endless approvals. And when mistakes happen? Instead of pointing fingers, everyone sees them as valuable chances to grow.
So, what practical habits make this action-first mindset work?
First, there’s the idea of small, quick experiments. Rather than rolling the dice on one big, risky plan, top-performing companies break challenges into bite-sized pieces. They’ll introduce a new idea on a small scale, see what happens, and if it works—they build on it.
Next, they rely on short feedback loops. By checking in with customers and employees early and often, they can spot issues before they snowball.
And they keep bureaucracy to a minimum. Streamlined processes and simple approval chains mean people aren’t stuck waiting for endless sign-offs. They can just get moving.
One of my favorite examples is the “do it, fix it, try it” approach you’ll see at some forward-thinking companies. Instead of holding out for the perfect answer, teams are urged to put a good-enough solution in place, see how it works, and then fine-tune from there. Not only does this speed up innovation, but it also helps employees feel more confident and invested in the outcome.
But there’s more to it than just moving fast. A bias for action creates real momentum. It energizes everyone, signaling that taking initiative is something to be proud of. It also helps teams become more resilient, since they’re used to facing uncertainty and making quick adjustments.
Of course, this isn’t about diving into chaos. The best organizations balance action with a clear sense of direction and shared values. Leaders set the boundaries and priorities, offering guidance without micromanaging every move.
So, here’s the key takeaway: When acting decisively becomes part of your culture, you create an environment where progress beats perfection, learning comes from doing, and everyone feels empowered to make a difference. Over time, this habit becomes a true engine for lasting excellence.
